subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which year did Vikings raid the monastery at Lindisfarne?
questions.explain: The raid on Lindisfarne in 793 is traditionally seen as the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

questions.q: From which region of Europe did the Vikings originate?
questions.explain: The Vikings came from the Scandinavian lands of Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

questions.q: What type of ship allowed the Vikings to raid coastlines and sail up rivers?
questions.explain: The shallow-draughted longship let Vikings make fast coastal raids and travel far inland along rivers.

questions.q: In Viking society, what name was given to the lowest class of enslaved people?
questions.explain: Viking society was divided into jarls (nobles), karls (free people) and thralls (slaves).

questions.q: The large Viking force that invaded England in 865 was known as the...?
questions.explain: The Great Heathen Army arrived in 865 and conquered much of northern and eastern England.

questions.q: Which Anglo-Saxon king defeated the Viking leader Guthrum at the Battle of Edington in 878?
questions.explain: Alfred of Wessex defeated Guthrum at Edington in 878, after which Guthrum was baptised as a Christian.

questions.q: What was the Viking name for the city of York, which became a major Viking settlement?
questions.explain: York, known to the Vikings as Jorvik, became a thriving centre of trade and Viking power.

questions.q: In which year did the Danish leader Cnut become king of England?
questions.explain: Cnut became king of England in 1016 and later ruled a North Sea empire including Denmark and Norway.

questions.q: What was the name for the payments of silver made to the Vikings to persuade them to stop attacking?
questions.explain: Danegeld was the tribute of silver paid, especially under Æthelred the Unready, to buy off Viking attackers.

questions.q: Why were monasteries such as Lindisfarne attractive targets for early Viking raids?
options: They held valuable treasures and were poorly defended
They had strong stone walls and armed soldiers
They were located far inland and hard to reach
They regularly paid the Vikings tribute
questions.explain: Coastal monasteries were rich in gold, silver and relics yet had few defences, making them easy targets.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why Vikings began to leave Scandinavia to raid and settle abroad?
options: Population growth and limited good farmland pushed them to seek land and wealth
Their homelands had been conquered by the Romans
They were fleeing a great plague in Scandinavia
They were ordered to leave by the Pope
questions.explain: Pressure on land at home, combined with the lure of wealth and trade, drove Viking expansion.

questions.q: What did the agreement between Alfred and Guthrum in the 880s establish?
options: A boundary dividing England, with Danish law applying in the north and east
Full Viking control over the whole of England
The complete expulsion of all Vikings from Britain
A united Christian kingdom ruled by Guthrum
questions.explain: The treaty fixed a frontier, leaving the north and east under Danish law in the area known as the Danelaw.

questions.q: Place names ending in '-by', such as Derby and Grimsby, are evidence of what?
questions.explain: The Old Norse ending '-by' meaning farm or village marks where Vikings settled, especially in the Danelaw.

questions.q: Why were the Five Boroughs (Derby, Leicester, Lincoln, Nottingham and Stamford) significant?
options: They were fortified towns that formed key centres of Viking settlement and power
They were Anglo-Saxon cathedral cities loyal to Wessex
They were Norman strongholds built after 1066
questions.explain: The Five Boroughs were important fortified centres of Danish rule and organisation within the Danelaw.

questions.q: What was one consequence of Æthelred the Unready repeatedly paying Danegeld?
options: It encouraged further Viking attacks as they returned for more silver
It permanently ended all Viking raids on England
It made the English peasantry much wealthier
It peacefully united England and Denmark
questions.explain: Paying tribute showed the Vikings that raiding England was profitable, so they kept coming back for more.

questions.q: How did Cnut seek to rule England effectively after becoming king?
options: He governed using existing English laws and the Church, dividing England into earldoms
He expelled all Anglo-Saxons from the country
He moved the seat of government permanently to Denmark
questions.explain: Cnut ruled largely through established English institutions and the Church, which helped secure a stable reign.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the lasting Viking legacy in England?
options: Place names and everyday words of Norse origin in the English language
questions.explain: Many English place names and common words derive from Old Norse, a lasting legacy of Viking settlement.

questions.q: A historian finds a village called 'Grimsthorpe' in eastern England. What does the '-thorpe' ending most likely indicate?
options: It was a Viking or Scandinavian settlement or outlying farm
It was a Norman manor built after 1066
It was an ancient Celtic hillfort
questions.explain: The Old Norse ending '-thorpe', meaning a secondary or outlying settlement, is evidence of Viking place-naming.

questions.q: A source records a monk in 793 writing that 'never before has such terror appeared in Britain'. This most likely refers to...?
questions.explain: This reaction reflects the shock caused by the 793 Viking attack on the monastery at Lindisfarne.

questions.q: An English king in the early 1000s repeatedly hands over silver to avoid Viking attacks. Which king and policy does this best describe?
options: Cnut ruling a North Sea empire
questions.explain: Æthelred the Unready is associated with repeatedly paying large sums of Danegeld to Viking raiders.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) History (SHP) (J411) specification; Viking Expansion c750-c1050
